body:
# the contributor audit of strict nonvertex gains and two distinct obstructions

This audit does not certify unrestricted OC. It checks three concrete
auxiliary results and an additional exact consequence of one example.

## 1. Constructive gain over ordinary maximal depth: PASS

Source: `candidate 24ea9b953da308e9`.

The cancellation in equation (7) is exact for one common ambient integer
tilt: the anchored base combination is the candidate base. Separate
containing-ball centers have no effect on either directional widths or
section-area bounds. The actual Minkowski combination is inside the
candidate fiber, so the displacement between its selected inball center
and the ordinary deepest point is at most `2R`.

For normals with `u.v >= -rho/2`, at least one partner supplies the
homothetic cap copy of volume `delta`. Moving the candidate loses at most
`2 R L epsilon <= delta/2` over the entire selected submeasure. For the
remaining normals the move enlarges every selected cap, and an own-fiber
inball supplies the explicit positive slab gain. Both regimes use the
same point. Vertical caps contain the whole own fiber and the stated
`A <= V/2`, `G <= V/2` estimates apply. Larger containing caps contain
the through-point cap. This proves the statement for all closed caps.

The volume-and-radius inball estimate follows from the ordinary depth
bound and the uniform support-strip volume bound. No positive lower
bound on anchored coefficients is needed. Continuity or upper
semicontinuity yields each claimed maximum, and the constructive point
does not depend on attainment of any mixed-cap infimum.

The limited-cardinality equality classification correctly uses the
separately proved ordinary simplex rigidity. An additional zero-volume
base cannot lie in the convex hull of the positive bases, because the
actual positive Minkowski combination would give it positive volume.
Strict separation then makes all its candidates have zero depth.

The sole geometric label error in the example was corrected independently
from “trapezoid” to “pentagon”. The root reran
`supporting computation verify_nonvertex_strict_ordinary_depth_gain.py`: PASS.

The parity-deficit equations in
`candidate 5904b09673c3b836` follow by summing
separate lower bounds for the same global maximum, not by combining cap
mass at different centers. Their direction and factor `1/Gamma_d` are
correct. They do not turn a collapsing gain into a uniform one.

## 2. Zero forest slack with graph Helly number above four: PASS

Source: `candidate 588eabf65d9a1440`.

The lower envelope of the three affine profiles is concave and positive
on the specified quadrilateral. It gives an actual full-dimensional
polytope with exactly the eight specified integer fibers. Its four unique
parity roots and all four nontrivial set-equality forest edges check
exactly. The graph map is an affine isomorphism on the centroid graph.

Each of the five specified graph points has a strict integer exposing
normal. Each omitted graph point violates a displayed inequality valid
on those five points. The five vertex-deletion convex hulls consequently
give a direct Helly witness, independently of any finite-set Helly
characterization. The original graph claim is false, although all
selected midpoint identities hold. This is not a counterexample to OC.

The root reran `supporting computation verify_zero_forest_centroid_graph_obstruction.py`: PASS.
Its distinct-pair depth certificate correctly counts three distinct
fibers and applies to every ambient halfspace, including vertical ones.

## 3. A useful strengthening for the entire example family

In fact the example in Section 2 satisfies OC for every `R >= 0` and
every integer `d >= 1`, not just its recorded `d=2,R=1` instance.
Suppress the common factor `|K|`. Write

    a = (R+16/8)^d,
    b = (R+14/8)^d,
    c = (R+12/8)^d,
    f = (R+11/8)^d,
    e = (R+10/8)^d,
    l = (R+ 8/8)^d.

The total weight is `T = a+b+c+f+e+3l`. The largest own-fiber
certificate is `Gamma_d a`. At graph point 4 the two disjoint opposite
pairs give `Gamma_d S`, where `S=c+e+l`.

Convexity of the real function `x -> x^d` on the positive axis gives

    b <= (a+c)/2,       f <= (c+e)/2.

Therefore

    T <= (3/2)a + 2c + (3/2)e + 3l
       <= (3/2)a + (5/2)(c+e+l)
       <= 4 max(a,S).

The second inequality uses `c+2e >= l`, which follows from `c,e >= l`.
Thus one of the two explicit actual centroid candidates attains at least
`Gamma_d T/4`. All ordinary cap and pairing arguments retain the true
homothetic fiber positions. This result resolves this example family
only, and does not assert a general weighted forest theorem.

## 4. The single-fiber variation trap: PASS

Source: `candidate fd2a9bc72f818ad3`.

The four fixed closed caps cover the appropriate full integer fibers,
and their interval lengths are exactly the asserted values. Retained
symmetric odd blocks supply the matching lower bounds at deterministic
integer-fiber centers. The two opposing Minkowski inclusions freeze
every interior unit interval when all the others are held fixed, while
the endpoint inclusion permits exactly contained-interval shrinks.

Consequently the single-endpoint variation has constant absolute maximum
`3/2` and normalized value `3/[2(3+t)]`. The centered two-endpoint
variation has absolute maximum `t+1/2` and normalized value
`(1+2t)/[4(1+t)]`. The stated generalization to `2m` unit fibers has
the same explicit cap and symmetric-submeasure certificates. Zero-length
endpoints contribute no mass and remain covered. These are counterexamples
to unconditional coordinatewise surgery, with original depths above OC.

The general exposed-fiber replacement is geometrically valid: the new
hull is contained in the old one, contains every retained fiber, and its
exposed replacement section is exactly the chosen subbody. Its relative
versus full-dimensional qualification is necessary and is present.

No result audited here proves the unrestricted OC estimate.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
